dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
sotto_argomento: Deploy virtual machines to availability zones and availability sets
domanda: Contoso is designing an availability set named AS1 that will host a web tier in the East US region. Before creating AS1, the infrastructure team must document the platform limits. What is the maximum number of fault domains and update domains that a single availability set supports?
spiegazione: Correct: an availability set can have up to 3 fault domains and up to 20 update domains, and these settings cannot be changed after the availability set is created. Option A (2 and 5) states the common portal defaults, not the maximums - it is the classic distractor for this topic. Option C is wrong because 5 is not a valid fault domain maximum; fault domains are capped at 3 (and the managed-disk fault domain count is either 2 or 3 depending on the region). Option D uses the correct fault domain maximum but the default update domain count of 5 instead of the maximum of 20.
tags: availability set,fault domain,update domain,high availability,virtual machines

dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
sotto_argomento: Deploy virtual machines to availability zones and availability sets
domanda: A finance application runs on two Azure virtual machines that are deployed in the same availability set in the West Europe region. Management asks you to state the uptime commitment that this configuration qualifies for. Which service-level agreement applies?
spiegazione: Correct: creating two or more VMs within an availability set helps keep applications highly available and meets the 99.95% Azure SLA. Option A (99.5%) is the single-instance figure associated with a VM that uses Standard SSD disks, not an availability set. Option B (99.9%) is the single-instance figure for a VM using premium SSD or ultra disk for all OS and data disks - it applies to one VM, not to an availability set. Option D (99.99%) requires two or more instances spread across two or more availability zones; an availability set lives inside a single zone-agnostic regional deployment and does not reach that tier.

dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
sotto_argomento: Move a virtual machine to another resource group, subscription, or region
domanda: An availability set named AS1 in a resource group named RG1 contains three virtual machines: VM1, VM2, and VM3. A colleague attempts to move only VM1 to a resource group named RG2, and the operation is rejected. What must you do to relocate VM1 to RG2?
opzione_a: Deallocate VM1 and retry the move operation.
opzione_b: Move AS1 together with VM1, VM2, and VM3 in the same move operation.
opzione_c: Delete AS1, move VM1 to RG2, then re-create AS1 in RG2 and add VM1 to it.
opzione_d: Use Azure Resource Mover to move VM1 to RG2.
spiegazione: Correct: Microsoft documents that virtual machines in an availability set can't be moved individually. The availability set and every VM it contains must be included in the same move request, which also satisfies the dependent-resource rule that would otherwise raise MissingMoveDependentResources. Option A is wrong because deallocation does not lift this restriction - deallocation only matters for a VM integrated with a key vault for Azure Disk Encryption being moved to another resource group. Option C fails because you can't add an existing VM to an availability set after the VM is created, so VM1 could never rejoin the re-created set. Option D is wrong because Azure Resource Mover is the service for moving resources across Azure regions; a move between resource groups in the same region uses the standard Resource Manager move operation (Move-AzResource / az resource move).
tags: move resources,availability set,resource group,move limitations,virtual machines

dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
sotto_argomento: Move a virtual machine to another resource group, subscription, or region
domanda: While moving a virtual machine and its dependent resources from Subscription1 to Subscription2, the validation phase fails with an error stating that the subscription is not registered for a resource type. Both subscriptions belong to the same Microsoft Entra tenant and you have Owner on both. What should you do to resolve the error?
opzione_a: Register the resource provider for the resource type in Subscription2.
opzione_b: Request a quota increase for the virtual machine SKU in Subscription2.
opzione_c: Remove the read-only lock from the destination resource group.
opzione_d: Transfer billing ownership of Subscription2 so that both subscriptions share a billing account.
spiegazione: Correct: the destination subscription must be registered for the resource provider of the resource you are moving. This error commonly appears when the destination subscription has never used that resource type. You fix it with Register-AzResourceProvider -ProviderNamespace <namespace> or az provider register --namespace <namespace>. Option B is wrong because insufficient quota produces a quota/limit error, not a provider-registration error - quota is a separate pre-move check. Option C is wrong because a read-only lock produces a distinct failure indicating the resource can't be moved due to the lock, not a provider registration message. Option D is wrong because billing ownership is irrelevant here; the tenant requirement is already satisfied, and billing transfer only matters when the source and destination subscriptions live in different Microsoft Entra tenants.

dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
sotto_argomento: Deploy virtual machines to availability zones and availability sets
domanda: A virtual machine named VM1 was deployed as a zonal VM into availability zone 1 of the East US region. Capacity planning now requires VM1's workload to run in availability zone 3 of the same region. You must minimize administrative effort while meeting the requirement. What should you do?
opzione_a: Stop VM1, change the Availability zone property on the VM blade, and start VM1.
opzione_b: Deploy a new zonal virtual machine in availability zone 3 and migrate the workload to it.
opzione_c: Add VM1 to an availability set that spans availability zones 1 and 3.
opzione_d: Use Azure Resource Mover to move VM1 between availability zones.
spiegazione: Correct: zonal VMs can't be moved to a different availability zone. Microsoft states you must deploy a new zonal VM in the desired zone instead. Option A is wrong because the availability zone is fixed at creation and there is no editable zone property that lets you relocate an existing zonal VM; the Availability + scaling blade only exposes a regional-to-zonal move for nonzonal VMs. Option C is wrong on two counts: an availability set is a regional construct that does not span availability zones, and you can't add an existing VM to an availability set after creation. Option D is wrong because Azure Resource Mover moves resources across Azure regions; the regional-to-zonal workflow it powers applies to nonzonal (regional) single-instance VMs, not to relocating an already-zonal VM to another zone.

dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
sotto_argomento: Move a virtual machine to another resource group, subscription, or region
domanda: VM1 is a Windows virtual machine that is integrated with a key vault named KV1 to implement Azure Disk Encryption. As part of a billing consolidation, VM1 must be moved from Subscription1 to Subscription2. Both subscriptions are in the same Microsoft Entra tenant. What must you do before the move can succeed?
opzione_a: Deallocate VM1 and leave encryption enabled.
opzione_c: Move KV1 to Subscription2 before you move VM1.
opzione_d: Convert VM1 to server-side encryption with a customer-managed key.
spiegazione: Correct: a VM integrated with a key vault for Azure Disk Encryption can be moved to another resource group while in a deallocated state, but to move such a VM to another subscription you must disable encryption first (for example, Disable-AzVMDiskEncryption -ResourceGroupName demoRG -VMName VM1 -VolumeType all). Option A is the classic trap: deallocation is the requirement for a cross-resource-group move, not a cross-subscription move. Option C is wrong because moving the key vault first does not remove the cross-subscription encryption restriction, and it would leave VM1 referencing a vault outside its own subscription. Option D is wrong because the documented remediation is to disable Azure Disk Encryption, not to re-encrypt the disks with a different mechanism; changing the encryption model is a far larger operation and is not what the move limitation calls for.
tags: move resources,azure disk encryption,subscription,key vault,move limitations

dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
sotto_argomento: Move a virtual machine to another resource group, subscription, or region
domanda: A cross-subscription move of a virtual machine named VM1 fails immediately with the error code MissingMoveDependentResources. VM1 is attached to a network interface in RG-Network, uses managed disks in RG-Storage, and connects to a virtual network in RG-Network. All resources are in Subscription1 and must end up in Subscription2. What should you do first?
opzione_a: Move the network interface, managed disks, and virtual network into the same resource group as VM1, then move that resource group's resources to Subscription2 in a single operation.
opzione_b: Submit separate move operations for VM1, the network interface, the disks, and the virtual network, in that order.
opzione_c: Register the Microsoft.Compute and Microsoft.Network resource providers in Subscription2.
opzione_d: Create replacement network interfaces, disks, and a virtual network in Subscription2, then move VM1.
spiegazione: Correct: for a move across subscriptions, the resource and its dependent resources must be located in the same resource group and must be moved together. Microsoft describes this as a three-step process - first consolidate the dependent resources into one resource group with a resource-group move, then move that set to the target subscription, then optionally redistribute them in the target subscription. Option B is wrong because splitting the resources across separate move requests reproduces the same MissingMoveDependentResources error; a dependent resource must either already exist in the destination or be included in the same request. Option C is wrong because an unregistered provider raises a different error ('subscription isn't registered for a resource type'), not MissingMoveDependentResources. Option D is wrong because a VM in an existing virtual network can be moved to a new subscription only when the virtual network and all its dependent resources are moved as well - pre-creating replacements does not satisfy the dependency validation for VM1's current NIC and disks.

dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
sotto_argomento: Move a virtual machine to another resource group, subscription, or region
domanda: Your team is preparing to move several virtual machines from Subscription1 to Subscription2. Both subscriptions are in the same Microsoft Entra tenant. Which of the following characteristics prevent a virtual machine from being moved to another subscription with the standard Resource Manager move operation? Select all that apply. Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
opzione_a: The virtual machine was created from a Marketplace resource with a plan attached.
opzione_b: The virtual machine is a member of an availability set and is selected on its own.
opzione_c: The virtual machine uses Standard SSD managed disks for its OS and data disks.
opzione_d: The virtual machine is an Azure Spot (low-priority) virtual machine.
opzione_e: The virtual machine runs in a region that does not support availability zones.
spiegazione: Correct answers: (A) virtual machines created from Marketplace resources with plans attached can't be moved across subscriptions - the documented workaround is to deprovision and redeploy in the target subscription after accepting the Marketplace terms there. (B) virtual machines in an availability set can't be moved individually; the availability set and all of its VMs must move together. (D) low-priority virtual machines and low-priority virtual machine scale sets can't be moved across resource groups or subscriptions. Incorrect: (C) the managed disk tier is irrelevant to move support - Standard SSD, Premium SSD, and Standard HDD managed disks all move with the VM as dependent resources; the disk-related blocker is Azure Disk Encryption, not the disk SKU. (E) availability zone support in the source region has no bearing on a resource group or subscription move, because a move does not change the physical region of the resource.
tags: move resources,move limitations,marketplace plan,spot vm,availability set

dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
sotto_argomento: Move a virtual machine to another resource group, subscription, or region
domanda: Litware plans to relocate a workload from the North Europe region to the Sweden Central region and wants to use Azure Resource Mover wherever possible. Which resource types can Azure Resource Mover currently move across regions? Select all that apply. Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
opzione_d: Azure SQL databases and elastic pools
spiegazione: Correct answers: Azure Resource Mover currently supports moving Azure VMs and associated disks, encrypted VMs and disks, NICs, availability sets (A), Azure virtual networks, public IP addresses, network security groups (B), internal and public load balancers, and Azure SQL databases and elastic pools (D) across regions. Incorrect: (C) Azure Key Vault is not in the Resource Mover supported list; relocating a key vault to another region requires the service-specific relocation guidance. (E) Azure App Service plans are likewise not supported by Resource Mover; App Service has its own relocation guidance, and the App Service move limitations article covers only resource group and subscription moves. A useful exam anchor: Resource Mover supports VMs but explicitly does not support Azure Spot VMs, and public IP addresses are moved but their addresses are not retained across regions.
tags: azure resource mover,move region,supported resources,relocation,virtual machines

dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
sotto_argomento: Move a virtual machine to another resource group, subscription, or region
domanda: As part of a governance review, you must document the hard requirements that Azure Resource Manager enforces before a virtual machine can be moved from one subscription to another. Which of the following are genuine requirements? Select all that apply. Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
opzione_a: The source and destination subscriptions must exist within the same Microsoft Entra tenant.
opzione_b: The account performing the move must have Microsoft.Resources/subscriptions/resourceGroups/moveResources/action on the source resource group.
opzione_c: The destination subscription must be registered for the resource provider of the resource being moved.
opzione_d: The source and destination subscriptions must use the same Azure region.
opzione_e: The source and destination resource groups must have the same name.
spiegazione: Correct answers: (A) the source and destination subscriptions must exist within the same Microsoft Entra tenant; if the tenant IDs differ you must first transfer billing ownership or associate the subscription with the target tenant. (B) the account moving the resources needs at least Microsoft.Resources/subscriptions/resourceGroups/moveResources/action at the source resource group (and Microsoft.Resources/subscriptions/resourceGroups/write at the destination resource group). (C) the destination subscription must be registered for the resource provider of the resource you're moving, otherwise the move fails with a 'subscription isn't registered for a resource type' error. Incorrect: (D) subscriptions are global containers and are not scoped to a region; a move never changes the physical region of a resource, so region alignment is not a requirement. (E) resource group names are irrelevant to the move; in fact the source and destination resource groups must be different, and naming has no bearing on validation.

dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
sotto_argomento: Deploy virtual machines to availability zones and availability sets
domanda: You are producing a one-page reference card that summarizes the Azure Virtual Machines high-availability options for your operations team. Select the correct value for each item.
opzione_a: Maximum fault domains in an availability set: [2 | 3 | 20]
opzione_b: Maximum update domains in an availability set: [5 | 20 | 100]
opzione_c: SLA for two or more VMs across two or more availability zones: [99.9% | 99.95% | 99.99%]
opzione_d: SLA for two or more VMs in a single availability set: [99.9% | 99.95% | 99.99%]
spiegazione: Fault domains: each availability set can have up to 3 fault domains, which group VMs that share a common power source and network switch; 2 is the frequent portal default and 20 is the update domain maximum, so both are distractors. Update domains: each availability set can have up to 20 update domains, which group VMs that can be restarted at the same time during planned maintenance; 5 is a common default and 100 is not a valid value. Availability zone SLA: two or more VMs spread across two or more availability zones in the same region qualify for the highest VM uptime tier of 99.99%, because each zone has a distinct power source, network, and cooling. Availability set SLA: two or more VMs in an availability set meet the 99.95% Azure SLA - lower than zones because an availability set is still susceptible to shared infrastructure failures such as a datacenter-level network outage that spans multiple fault domains. 99.9% is the single-instance premium SSD / ultra disk figure and applies to neither multi-instance configuration.

dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
sotto_argomento: Move a virtual machine to another resource group, subscription, or region
domanda: Fabrikam is reorganizing its Azure estate. VM1 must be relocated from a resource group named RG1 to a resource group named RG2 in the same subscription and region. Separately, VM2 must be relocated from the East US region to the West Europe region. Select the correct answer for each item.
opzione_a: Tool to relocate VM1 from RG1 to RG2: [Azure Resource Mover | Move-AzResource | Azure Site Recovery]
opzione_b: Tool to relocate VM2 from East US to West Europe: [Azure Resource Mover | Move-AzResource | New-AzAvailabilitySet]
opzione_c: Effect of the RG1-to-RG2 move on the physical location of VM1: [Changes to the target region | Remains unchanged | Becomes zone-redundant]
opzione_d: Maximum time the source and destination resource groups stay locked during a move: [30 minutes | 4 hours | 24 hours]
spiegazione: Item 1: a move between resource groups in the same subscription uses the standard Resource Manager move operation - Move-AzResource in Az PowerShell (or az resource move in the Azure CLI). Azure Resource Mover is scoped to cross-region moves, and Azure Site Recovery is a business continuity and disaster recovery service, not a relocation tool for resource groups. Item 2: Azure Resource Mover is the purpose-built hub for moving resources such as VMs across Azure regions; Move-AzResource cannot change a resource's region, and New-AzAvailabilitySet simply creates an availability set. Item 3: moving a resource only changes its associated resource group and doesn't alter the physical region of the resource - this is the single most-tested fact about resource group moves. It also does not confer any zone redundancy. Item 4: Azure Resource Manager allows a move operation four hours to finish, and both the source and destination resource groups are locked for that period; most moves complete faster and the lock is removed accordingly. During the lock you can't create, delete, or update resources in either resource group, although existing resources keep running.
tags: move resources,azure resource mover,move-azresource,resource group lock,region

dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
sotto_argomento: Deploy virtual machines to availability zones and availability sets
domanda: An availability set named AS1 exists in the East US region. AS1 was created with a platform fault domain count of 2 and a platform update domain count of 5, and it currently contains two virtual machines named VM1 and VM2. A third virtual machine named VM3 already exists in the same region and resource group but is not a member of any availability set. Evaluate each of the following proposed statements and determine whether it is correct. 1) You can reconfigure AS1 to use 3 fault domains without re-creating the availability set. 2) You can add the existing VM3 to AS1 so that AS1 contains three virtual machines. 3) Running VM1 and VM2 inside AS1 qualifies the workload for the 99.95% Azure SLA.
opzione_a: You can reconfigure AS1 to use 3 fault domains without re-creating the availability set.
opzione_b: You can add the existing VM3 to AS1 so that AS1 contains three virtual machines.
opzione_c: Running VM1 and VM2 inside AS1 qualifies the workload for the 99.95% Azure SLA.
spiegazione: Statement 1 - No. Each availability set can have up to 3 fault domains and 20 update domains, but these settings can't be changed after the availability set is created. To use 3 fault domains you must create a new availability set with that fault domain count and deploy the VMs into it. Statement 2 - No. VMs must be created within the availability set so that Azure can distribute them correctly across the hardware; you can't add an existing VM to an availability set after it's created. VM3 would have to be redeployed as a member of AS1. Statement 3 - Yes. Using two or more VMs in an availability set helps keep applications highly available and meets the 99.95% Azure SLA. There's no extra cost for the availability set itself; you only pay for each VM instance.

dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
sotto_argomento: Move a virtual machine to another resource group, subscription, or region
domanda: Northwind Traders has two Azure subscriptions named Subscription1 and Subscription2 that belong to the same Microsoft Entra tenant. A resource group named RG1 in Subscription1 contains a virtual machine named VM1 and its dependent resources. An Azure role assignment for a support engineer is scoped directly to VM1. You plan to relocate the workload to Subscription2. Evaluate each of the following proposed statements and determine whether it is correct. 1) You can move RG1 itself into Subscription2 so that RG1 and everything it contains ends up in Subscription2. 2) The role assignment scoped to VM1 moves with VM1 to the destination resource group. 3) A single move operation can include a maximum of 800 resources.
opzione_a: You can move RG1 itself into Subscription2 so that RG1 and everything it contains ends up in Subscription2.
opzione_b: The role assignment scoped to VM1 moves with VM1 to the destination resource group.
opzione_c: A single move operation can include a maximum of 800 resources.
spiegazione: Statement 1 - No. You can't move a resource group to a new subscription. You can move all of the resources in a resource group to a resource group in another subscription, but the resource group object itself stays put, and settings such as tags, role assignments, and policies don't transfer automatically to the destination resource group. Statement 2 - No. If you move a resource with an active Azure role assignment, the role assignment doesn't move and becomes orphaned. You must create the role assignment again after the move; Microsoft recommends removing the orphaned assignment before the move. Statement 3 - Yes. Resource Manager immediately returns an error when there are more than 800 resources in a single operation, and Microsoft recommends separating large moves into different operations because even fewer than 800 resources can fail by timing out.

dominio: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
sotto_argomento: Move a virtual machine to another resource group, subscription, or region
domanda: Case study: Fabrikam runs a three-tier application in the East US region under a subscription named Subscription1. The web tier consists of VM1, VM2, and VM3 in an availability set named AS1. The data tier consists of a single virtual machine named VM4, which is protected by Azure Backup in a Recovery Services vault; soft delete is enabled on the vault, and instant restore snapshots are stored in a resource group named AzureBackupRG_eastus_1. Following an acquisition, Fabrikam must move all compute resources to a subscription named Subscription2, which is in the same Microsoft Entra tenant. The workload must remain in East US. Your first attempt to move VM4 to Subscription2 fails. What should you do to enable the move of VM4?
opzione_a: Stop the backup while keeping backup data, delete the Restore Point Collection for VM4 from AzureBackupRG_eastus_1, and if soft delete keeps the restore points, disable soft delete or wait 14 days.
opzione_b: Delete the Recovery Services vault that protects VM4, then move VM4 and re-create the vault in Subscription2.
opzione_c: Convert VM4 from a zonal to a nonzonal configuration, then retry the move.
opzione_d: Move the Recovery Services vault and AzureBackupRG_eastus_1 to Subscription2 first, then move VM4.
spiegazione: Correct: to move virtual machines configured with Azure Backup you must delete the restore point collections (instant recovery snapshots) from the vault - the documented flow is to temporarily stop the backup while keeping backup data, delete the resource of type Restore Point Collection named AzureBackup_<VM name>_########### (by default in AzureBackupRG_<VM location>_1), then move the VM and reconfigure backup. Deleting that resource removes only the instant recovery points, not the backed-up data in the vault. Because soft delete is enabled, Microsoft explicitly states you can't move the VM while those restore points are kept, so you must either disable soft delete or wait 14 days after deleting the restore points. Option B is wrong and destructive: deleting the vault is never the documented remediation, would discard the protected backup data, and is unnecessary because restore points already copied to the vault can be retained and moved. Option C is wrong because the case study never places VM4 in an availability zone, and zonal configuration is not a blocker for a subscription move - a move does not alter the physical region or zone of a resource. Option D is wrong because moving the vault does not clear the instant restore point collections that block the VM move; furthermore, moving a Recovery Services vault has its own separate restrictions and does not address the soft delete condition.
tags: move resources,azure backup,restore point collection,soft delete,subscription
